body: I can confirm the issue, it's a regression from 4.7 dev 4. I'll bisect.
Reverting PR #118080 fixes the issue. CC @mihe
@matheusmdx Thank you for confirming the bug. Can you advise me with some sort of simple workaround for 4.7 to achieve the desired behaviour of the nerf darts?

> [@matheusmdx](https://github.com/matheusmdx) Thank you for confirming the bug. Can you advise me with some sort of simple workaround for 4.7 to achieve the desired behaviour of the nerf darts?

What i can think is use an `Area2D` and move it manually if you don't need nothing more than the darts fly straight and detect collision.

@matheusmdx What I'm tring to achieve: in my scene are several RigidBody2Ds, some are also moving. When the Nerf Dart hits another RigidBody2D, it should bounce off and continue  flying, like a rubber ball hitting a wall and bouncing away.

Using physics for this is very convenient, because the physics engine already does all the heavy lifting: just give an impulse, the engine handles collision and bouncing.
I tried follwoing your advice and create somethin similiar at the weekend but was dissatisfied with the result. :(

I also think maybe I'm doing it wrong and misunderstand using physics. An obvious change in behaviour between versions like this should be spotted by many devs, but there seems to be only me. So maybe everyone else is doing this different and in a better way, but currently I'm unable to figure this out.

> Reverting PR [#118080](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/118080) fixes the issue. CC [@mihe](https://github.com/mihe)

This doesn't really seem to be a bug/regression, as far as I can tell. The problem is this part of `nerf_dart.gd`:

```gd
## Match Rotation to Velocity-Direction
func _process(_delta: float) -> void:
	rotation = linear_velocity.angle()
```

Setting `rotation` on a `RigidBody2D` continuously like that, especially in `_process`, is known to be problematic, as you end up fighting against the physics engine in a number of ways. This is already called out (somewhat vaguely) in [the documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_rigidbody2d.html) for `RigidBody2D`:

> **Note:** Changing the 2D transform or linear_velocity of a RigidBody2D very often may lead to some unpredictable behaviors.

(Changing `rotation` in this case is what changes the 2D transform.)

I haven't done a deep dive to see what exactly the data race ends up being in this case, nor why you were able to get away with this prior to Godot 4.7, but commenting out that code seems to resolve the issue, as far as the darts getting stuck.

Moving the setting of `rotation` to `_physics_process` also technically seems to resolve the problem, but again, I would not recommend setting `rotation` (or any part of the transform) continuously like that to begin with.

Judging by your comment I assume that code is meant to force the dart to always point along its trajectory? Would it work to instead use something like a `CircleShape2D` for the dart and then set the rotation of the `Sprite2D` instead? That way you don't have to do anything to the `RigidBody2D` at all.

If you need a more precise shape than a `CircleShape2D`, you'll likely need to apply some kind of torque to the body based on the difference from the current angle to `linear_velocity.angle()`, instead of setting `rotation` like you are now, which can be tricky to get right.

To anyone who is interested in a workaround: after realizing I'm fighting the physics engine I did these changes.

nerf_dart.tscn:
In the RigidBody2D  set lock_rotation=true

In nerf_dart.gd
Removed :
_process(delta)

Added:
```
func _physics_process(_delta: float) -> void:
	if abs(rotation - linear_velocity.angle()) > 0.5:
		print("Rotation needs fixing: ", rotation, " vs ", linear_velocity.angle())
		rotation = linear_velocity.angle()

func _integrate_forces(state: PhysicsDirectBodyState2D) -> void:
	pass
	# Highly unexpected: planned to use state.angular_velocity = 0 here, but it works anyway

```
Observed Behavoiur:
Nerf Dart always points to trajectory path, even after colliding with other RigidBody2Ds.
Nerf Dart flys with out hitting another RigidBody2D: print() is never called
Nerf Dart flys with hitting another RigidBody2D: Nerf Dart bounces, print() is called once
Nerf Dart flys with hitting multiple RigidBody2D: Nerf Dart bounces, print() is called for every bounce

Nice, just what I wanted!

@mihe I got it working thanks to your input but I found another astonishing thing I would like to bring to your attention.See my post above. Before this I added to nerf_dart.gd

```
func _integrate_forces(state: PhysicsDirectBodyState2D) -> void:
	if state.angular_velocity != 0:
		print("Angular velocity needs fixing: ", state.angular_velocity)

	state.angular_velocity = 0
```
But the print() was never executed, which would make sense because lock_rotation=true.
But after removing _integrate_forces() I got multiple "print("Rotation needs fixing:...)" from _physics_process() after the dart collided with an obstacle.

Adding 
```
func _integrate_forces(state: PhysicsDirectBodyState2D) -> void:
	pass
```
changed this back to the behaviour, where "print("Rotation needs fixing:...)" was just called once per collision.
It's very strange that doing nothing in _integrate_forces() and just having an empty implementation causes a change of behaviour.
But physics is complicated stuff...

I'm not complaining and would rather not open an issue for this. If you are interested in looking into this behaviour, I provided an updated version of my test project that also has some obstacles for the dart to bounce of.
